subject: 🏃 Saturday — Easy Shakeout or Bike (Wk 3)
html:
Tomorrow: Game-time call — 3 mi easy shakeout OR 30–45 min easy bike. This is a flush before Sunday's 10 mi long run, not a workout. Pick the run if legs feel fresh; pick the bike if anything is barking or you want the variety. Either way, keep it strictly easy.

If you run: 3 mi flat @ 9:15–9:30, HR cap 145. Do the 5-min pre-run activation first (hip CARs, banded lateral walks, glute bridges, quadruped banded hip IR 5–10 reps each side). Bayfront or flat neighborhood loop — no hills.

If you bike: 30–45 min, HR cap 130 (Z1/low Z2). Flat route, easy gear, seated on the climbs. The May 16 pre-B2B bike (avg HR 102, max 125) is the template — that dose was perfect.

Focus cue: Quiet legs. The goal is blood flow and a gentle range-of-motion check, nothing more. If you catch yourself pushing to 8:30 pace or grinding a hill on the bike, you're doing it wrong. Save the legs — Sunday's 10-miler is the session that matters this weekend.

PT block makeup: You skipped the side plank, dead bug, and chin tuck today due to time — that's two Fridays in a row. Do them at home tonight or tomorrow morning before the shakeout. Five minutes, no equipment beyond a band. Those are PT-prescribed and non-negotiable.

Context: Week 3 of 12, Phase 1 Foundation — 64 days to race day. Strong week: Thursday's compressed progression hit 7:29 at HR 161 (threshold, clean), today's Bulgarians progressed to 25 lb/hand with knee 1/5. Five straight sessions at 1/5 since the B2B recovery. Sunday's 10 mi long run is flat Bayfront @ 8:45–9:15 — pure aerobic time-on-feet. PAL 10K is one week out.

Tonight: Hydrate well, carb-forward dinner (rice bowl, pasta, sweet potato). Bed by 10. H10 strap charged and ready for Sunday's long run — that's the data we need clean.
